title: Kummer restriction triangle: derived concentration and tensor-unit Tor bound
statement:
Fix $k,\ell,E,n,A$ in the finite-coefficient setting of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and suppose $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$. Use $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $p:X\to Y$, the zero section $s$, its open complement $j:U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow X$, $\pi=pj$, the twist $A(1)$, and $\kappa(t)\in H^1(U,A(1))$ from [def-pur-affine-line-datum]. All sheaves and derived categories are ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $P=Rp_*A_X(1)[0]$ and $Q=R\pi_*A_U(1)[0]$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let
$$B_0\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{r}Q\xrightarrow{\delta}B_0[1]$$
be any distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category] whose second arrow is derived restriction along $j$, with the canonical direct-image composition identification [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. Use cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and put $C_0=B_0[2]$.

The unit $A_Y(1)[0]\to P$ is an isomorphism, $\mathcal H^0(r)$ is an isomorphism, $P$ has no cohomology outside degree zero, and $Q$ has no cohomology outside degrees zero and one. Let $\gamma:A_Y\to\mathcal H^1(Q)$ be the map sending $1$ to the edge image of $\kappa(t)$. The connecting map of this triangle gives an isomorphism $\delta^1:\mathcal H^1(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^2(B_0)$, and $\gamma$ is an isomorphism. There is a derived isomorphism
$$\theta:A_Y[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}C_0$$
whose degree-zero cohomology map, under $\mathcal H^0(C_0)=\mathcal H^2(B_0)$, is exactly $\delta^1\gamma$. More precisely the canonical good-truncation isomorphism $C_0\cong\mathcal H^0(C_0)[0]$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] induces the identity on $\mathcal H^0$; composing its inverse with $(\delta^1\gamma)[0]$ gives $\theta$. In particular $\mathcal H^m(B_0)=0$ for $m\ne2$, and $C_0$ has constant lisse rank-one degree-zero cohomology and no other cohomology. Moreover $C_0\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For every degree-zero module sheaf $M$, there is an isomorphism $C_0\otimes_A^L M[0]\cong M[0]$ induced by $\theta$ and the tensor unit [def-weil-derived-tensor], so its Tor interval is $[0,0]$.

source.place: First paragraph, units and Kummer generator, long exact sequence, shift, good truncation and finite-Tor conclusion; returned steps 3-6.

proof.text: The coefficient module categories on the chosen small pro-etale sites are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], applied to the constant ring sheaves. Both direct images are additive and left exact by [lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] with $b=0$ to the degree-zero sheaves $A_X(1)$ and $A_U(1)$. Thus $\mathcal H^m(P)=\mathcal H^m(Q)=0$ for $m<0$. The total derived images here restrict to the bounded-below right derived functors used by that lemma, computed by the same injective resolutions.

source.place: Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing (1), applied to degree-zero module sheaves

proof.text: Apply [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](1)-(3), with $\Lambda=A$ and precisely the specified pro-etale Kummer class. It gives the unit $u_p:A_Y(1)[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}P$, $\mathcal H^m(Q)=0$ for $m\ge2$, and the isomorphism $\gamma:A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^1(Q)$ sending $1$ to the edge image of $\kappa(t)$. Its clause (2) identifies the degree-zero unit for $\pi$ with restriction composed with $p^*$: $u_\pi^0=\mathcal H^0(r)\mathcal H^0(u_p)$. Both units are invertible, so $\mathcal H^0(r)=u_\pi^0\mathcal H^0(u_p)^{-1}$ is invertible. Since $u_p$ identifies $P$ with a degree-zero sheaf, $P$ vanishes cohomologically outside zero. Together with step 1 this gives every claimed bound on $P,Q$.

source.place: First paragraph: restriction triangle and its cohomology

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] for the given triangle, without rotating it. Its degree-zero segment, since $\mathcal H^{-1}(Q)=0$, is $0\to\mathcal H^0(B_0)\to\mathcal H^0(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0(Q)\to\mathcal H^1(B_0)\to0$. Exactness makes the kernel and cokernel of this isomorphism zero, hence $\mathcal H^0(B_0)=\mathcal H^1(B_0)=0$. The next segment is $0=\mathcal H^1(P)\to\mathcal H^1(Q)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}\mathcal H^2(B_0)\to\mathcal H^2(P)=0$, so the actual connecting map $\delta^1$ is an isomorphism.

For $m<0$ or $m\ge3$, the same exact sequence has segment $\mathcal H^{m-1}(Q)\to\mathcal H^m(B_0)\to\mathcal H^m(P)$ with both outer objects zero, so $\mathcal H^m(B_0)=0$. Together with step 3 this leaves only degree two. The cochain shift convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $\mathcal H^i(C_0)=\mathcal H^{i+2}(B_0)$; hence $C_0=B_0[2]$ is concentrated in degree zero, and $\delta^1\gamma:A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0(C_0)$.

source.place: Tag 0147, long exact sequence; cochain shift convention preceding lemma-cohomology-homological

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization] to $C_0$ in the abelian category of $A_Y$-module sheaves. Its canonical isomorphism $\epsilon:C_0\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0(C_0)[0]$ is $Q(p_K)Q(c_K)^{-1}$ on any representative $K$. On $H^0$, $c_K$ identifies cycles modulo boundaries with the same quotient, and $p_K$ sends a cycle to its class, so $H^0(\epsilon)$ is the identity under the canonical single-complex comparison. Define $\theta=\epsilon^{-1}\circ(\delta^1\gamma)[0]$. This is a derived isomorphism and its degree-zero map is exactly $\delta^1\gamma$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations: canonical cochain truncation at zero, cycle-to-cohomology quotient

proof.text: By step 5 the only cohomology sheaf of $C_0$ is the constant sheaf $A_Y$, which is already globally free of rank one. Thus it is lisse. The one stratum $Y$ and the finite module $A$ satisfy [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] (use the empty partition if $Y$ is empty); hence $C_0\in D^b_c(Y,A)$. No conclusion is inferred merely from fibre ranks.

source.place: First paragraph: restriction triangle and its cohomology

proof.text: The sheaf tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $A_Y\otimes_{A_Y}F\cong F$ by $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$, inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; these sectionwise mutually inverse maps sheafify and commute with restrictions. Consequently the total tensor of $A_Y[0]$ with any complex $F^\bullet$ is that same complex, degree by degree, with the same differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In particular it sends acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes, so $A_Y[0]$ is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: First paragraph: restriction triangle and its cohomology

proof.text: For any degree-zero module sheaf $M$, use the K-flat representative $A_Y[0]$ in [def-weil-derived-tensor] to compute $A_Y[0]\otimes_A^L M[0]\cong M[0]$ by step 7. Tensoring the inverse of $\theta$ gives $C_0\otimes_A^L M[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Y[0]\otimes_A^L M[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}M[0]$. It has cohomology only in degree zero for every $M$, so [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] gives the Tor interval $[0,0]$. With step 6 this proves $C_0\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$.
